subject: Can I rotate the factor structure in multipleGroup function?

messages.author: 6a75f6f91a59c568
messages.subject: Can I rotate the factor structure in multipleGroup function?
parts:
Dear Phil,

Can I rotate the factor structure in multipleGroup function?

Like this:

> dat1 <- expand.table(LSAT6)
> dat2 <- expand.table(LSAT7)
> dat <- data.frame(dat1, dat2)
> dat$group <- c(rep('D1', 500), rep('D2', 500))
> multipleGroup(dat[1:10], 2, group=as.factor(dat$group), method = "MHRM", rotate='geominQ', technical=list(NCYCLES=999999, MAXQUAD=9999999999999))

Best wishes,
Seongho Bae

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Can I rotate the factor structure in multipleGroup function?
parts:
Hi Seongho,

Not directly unfortunately since I generally believe multiple group models should be confirmatory in nature. It's hard to justify what the structural differences between groups are when within group structure is pretty much unknown. What you've presented here is essentially two single group models that have simply been pasted together in estimation (if you estimate each group separately and add the log-likelihoods together you'll obtain the same result), so I would recommend just treating them separately with mirt().

However, if you do end up including things like between group equality constraints then you'll have to extract and re-class the models in order for rotation to work (I don't normally suggest doing this, but it works here). E.g.

mod <- multipleGroup(....)
group1mod <- mod@pars[[1L]]
class(group1mod) <- 'ExploratoryClass'
summary(group1mod, rotate = 'oblimin') 
group2mod <- mod@pars[[2L]]
class(group2mod) <- 'ExploratoryClass'
summary(group2mod, rotate = 'oblimin') 

Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Can I rotate the factor structure in multipleGroup function?
parts:
I've added a safer way to extract single group objects from multipleGroup() definitions through a new extract.group() function. It can be use this way, and now detect whether the parameters should be in the exploratory class family or not. Cheers.

Phil

```
# requires mirt 1.4.6+

group <- factor(c(rep('D1', 500), rep('D2', 500)))
mod <- multipleGroup(dat, 2, group=group)

g1 <- extract.group(mod, 1)
g2 <- extract.group(mod, 2)
summary(g1, rotate = 'oblimin')
summary(g1, rotate = 'promax')
```
